AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-23

Generated: 2026-11-23 01:33 UTC | Tools covered: 7

  • OpenAI Codex
  • Gemini CLI
  • GitHub Copilot CLI
  • OpenCode

Cross-Tool Comparison

Cross-Tool Comparison Report: AI CLI Ecosystem

Date: 2026-11-23 | Coverage: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, Qwen Code

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI CLI tooling landscape in late 2026 has entered a stabilization-and-hardening phase rather than a pure feature race. Every major tool reported zero or near-zero new releases in the last 24 hours, yet all seven trackers showed heavy issue activity — a signature of mature products absorbing a wave of regressions from recent architectural migrations (V1→V2 agent models, managed-service layers, persistent-PTY transports). The dominant cross-cutting themes are subagent orchestration reliability, permission/sandbox correctness, context/token cost transparency, and cross-platform parity (especially Windows). Security defaults that over-block legitimate work and silent failures (dropped files, misreported success states) have emerged as the most trust-damaging bug classes across the ecosystem. Meanwhile, a clear architectural convergence is underway around MCP as the universal tool-integration layer and agents-invoking-agents as the next capability frontier.

2. Activity Comparison

Tool Issues (updated 24h) PRs (updated 24h) Discussions Release Status
Claude Code ~50 updated 1 (open) N/A (none in dataset) No release
OpenAI Codex High (~10+ hot) ~13 (all closed/merged) 12 (6 Ideas, 3 Q&A, 5 Show-and-tell) No release
Gemini CLI 10 hot (multiple P1) ~12 (ACP-heavy) N/A (none in dataset) v0.71.0 nightly
GitHub Copilot CLI 19 updated 2 (1 open, 1 closed) N/A (none in dataset) v1.0.115-7
OpenCode 10 hot (high engagement) 10 (mixed open/closed) N/A (none in dataset) No release
Pi 10 hot (untriaged regressions) 3 (all closed, 0 open) 1 Show-and-tell No release (stable 1.6.0)
Qwen Code 10 hot (CI-dominated) 10 (feature-heavy) N/A (none in dataset) v0.28.4 CLI + Desktop

Notes:

  • Discussions = N/A for Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, and Qwen Code — these repos primarily route community input through Issues and PRs. This reflects channel design, not inactivity.
  • OpenAI Codex is the only tool with a robust, actively curated Discussions surface (12 threads in 24h).
  • Gemini CLI and Copilot CLI and Qwen Code shipped releases; the rest held steady, consistent with post-release stabilization.

3. Shared Feature Directions

Requirements echoing across multiple communities — the strongest signal of genuine ecosystem-wide demand:

a. Subagent Orchestration & Observability (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Copilot CLI, Pi)

  • OpenCode is the epicenter: foreground subagent execution restoration (#64073, 25 comments) and a live subagent sidebar (#41249) dominate.
  • Gemini CLI wants agents to invoke other agents (#30409, #28738) with depth limits, plus subagent trajectory visibility (#22598).
  • Copilot CLI reports nested subagents silently can't run multi-turn (#5543).
  • Pi flags blind tool-call concurrency causing stale reads (#11950).
  • Claude Code sees MCP elicitation auto-declined in VS Code (#98256). → Users want delegated work to be visible, controllable, and correctly reported.

b. Permission / Sandbox Boundary Correctness (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Pi)

  • Claude Code: blanket password-typing block (#78160, 25 comments) and false-positive reasoning_extraction blocks (#111336).
  • OpenAI Codex: UI shows "Full access" but executor enforces read-only (#62926, #62975); approval races turn lifecycle (#60139).
  • Pi: --tools scoping silently undone by tool registration (#12399) — security-adjacent. → Trust boundaries are either over-blocking legit work or under-enforcing declared policy.

c. Context / Token Cost Transparency (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, OpenCode, Qwen Code)

  • Claude Code: desktop 79k vs 13k CLI context overhead (#105328); warm-cache rewrites (#91514).
  • OpenAI Codex: subagent prompt-cache lineage loss (#24704, 👍20).
  • OpenCode: keep.tokens ignored at 234K vs 15K (#43250); expensive compaction re-prefill (#65549).
  • Qwen Code: top_k missing from telemetry (#18106). → Opaque metering and cache-miss re-prefill translate directly into cost and latency surprises.

d. Persistent / Cross-Session Memory (OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Pi)

  • Codex: "continuous engineering workspace" across ChatGPT/Work/Codex (#61348, 41 comments).
  • Gemini CLI: file-based persistent tasks (#18836) to fight context rot.
  • Qwen Code: share auto-memory across Git worktrees (#18030).
  • Pi: permanent conversation deletion (#11026) and session lifecycle hygiene.

e. Windows & Non-Default Environment Parity (Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Copilot CLI, Pi, Qwen Code)

  • Claude Code: case-sensitive drive-letter worktree bug (#91618); Windows Terminal input loss (#111754).
  • Codex: Windows permission cluster is its dominant pain point.
  • Copilot CLI: Schannel TLS failure on managed networks (#5546).
  • Pi: custom Git-for-Windows install not found (#12408).
  • Qwen Code: silent @-path dropping on Windows (#18141). → Five of seven tools have active Windows-specific defects — clearly under-tested.

f. MCP Reliability & Capability Parity (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, OpenCode)

  • Claude Code: elicitation auto-declined, missing headers, GitHub MCP not loading.
  • Codex: MCP tool-list change subscriptions (#62681).
  • Copilot CLI: built-in GitHub MCP tools hidden when gh on PATH (#5550).
  • OpenCode: silent 61-tool MCP truncation (#65590, fixed).

4. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension Claude Code OpenAI Codex Gemini CLI Copilot CLI OpenCode Pi Qwen Code
Target user Pro devs, Max subscribers Cross-surface engineering teams Agent-architecture experimenters GitHub-centric enterprise teams Open-source / TUI power users Multi-agent power users (Bedrock/Google) Self-hosted / open-weight adopters
Core focus Safety defaults + Max-tier scale Continuous workspace + desktop UX Agent subsystem & ACP hardening Cloud sessions + agent tooling V2 migration parity + TUI polish Agent SDK correctness + provider adapters Web Shell + managed-agent infra
Technical approach Sandbox/worktree isolation, aggressive safety blocks Cloud+local hybrid, subagent cache optimization ACP/A2A protocol, AST-aware tooling ACP, --ui-server, MCP built-ins Persistent-PTY, service architecture Harness SDK, contribution-gated fixes CI-as-product, deflake automation
Signature 2026-11 pain False-positive safeguards, TUI input loss Windows permission enforcement Subagent hangs / misreported success Cloud session reconnection V1→V2 regression loss Post-1.6.0 adapter regressions CI flakiness, silent failures
Community channel Issues-only Issues + rich Discussions Issues + PRs Issues + PRs Issues + PRs Issues + light Discussions Issues + PRs

Distinct personalities:

  • Claude Code optimizes for safety-first defaults — and is now paying for over-blocking.
  • Codex is the most complete product surface (desktop → mobile → cloud), but Windows enforcement is its Achilles' heel.
  • Gemini CLI is the most architecturally ambitious, betting on ACP/A2A and agent-invoking-agents.
  • Copilot CLI is the enterprise/GitHub-native play, but cloud session reliability lags.
  • OpenCode is the open-source TUI purist, wrestling with V2 migration debt.
  • Pi is the harness/SDK specialist, notably dependent on provider-adapter correctness (Bedrock, Google, Copilot).
  • Qwen Code is the self-hosted/open-weight champion, with an unusually mature CI-as-product discipline.

5. Community Momentum & Maturity

Tool Momentum Maturity Evidence
OpenAI Codex ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ High 85-comment issue; 12 curated Discussions; 13 merged PRs/day; one closed macOS regression
Gemini CLI ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Rapid iteration Multiple P1s under retest; coherent ACP PR swarm from one contributor; nightly cadence
OpenCode ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Mid-migration 25-comment flagship thread; balanced issue+PR load; V2 parity still being clawed back
Claude Code ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Very mature 50 issues/day but only 1 PR — high user base, lower merge velocity visible externally
Pi ⭐⭐⭐ Stabilizing Post-1.6.0 regression wave; contribution-gate friction stalling ready fixes (#8643)
Qwen Code ⭐⭐⭐ Infra-heavy CI-dominated tracker; two releases shipped; Web Shell fastest-moving surface
Copilot CLI ⭐⭐ Early-stabilizing 19 issue updates but only 2 PRs; cloud-session bugs freshly reported

Key observations:

  • Codex and Gemini CLI are the most actively iterating — high PR throughput with visible architectural direction.
  • Claude Code has the largest visible signal volume but the thinnest PR flow in this window — a pattern consistent with internal development and external issue triage.
  • Pi shows a process bottleneck: multiple high-👍 fixes (#8643, #12184) wait on contribution-gate review, a maturity risk.
  • Qwen Code is unusual in treating CI reliability as a first-class product surface — deflake bots, bounded-poll fixes, autofix approvals.

6. Trend Signals

Trend 1 — The agent is the new unit of complexity

Every community is simultaneously adding agent-invokes-agent capability and fighting the resulting reliability gaps (hangs, misreported success, cache lineage loss, stale reads). Reference value: teams adopting multi-agent workflows should invest early in observability and turn-budget reporting, not just capability.

Trend 2 — Safety defaults are being renegotiated

Password-typing blocks, reasoning_extraction false positives, "Full access" that isn't, and --tools scoping leaks all point the same direction: users want permission-gated opt-in escapes, not hard blocks. Reference value: ship configurable trust boundaries with safe defaults, or users will route around the tool.

Trend 3 — Cost/context transparency is a competitive feature

Desktop context overhead, cache-miss re-prefill, ignored keep.tokens, and missing telemetry fields appear across four communities. Reference value: honest token accounting and reliable compaction are now table-stakes for power-user retention.

Trend 4 — Cross-platform parity is unfinished business

Windows and non-default environments (Wayland, custom installs, corporate TLS, split-DNS) break in five of seven tools. Reference value: if you're deploying to mixed-OS fleets, budget for platform-specific QA on every release.

Trend 5 — MCP is consolidating as the integration spine

Four tools surfaced MCP-specific bugs the same day (elicitation, tool-list subscriptions, gh-on-PATH shadowing, 61-tool truncation). Reference value: MCP is now the assumed extension layer — treat its reliability the way you'd treat a core dependency.

Trend 6 — Silent failures are the most damaging bug class

Dropped file attachments, hidden MCP tools, disposed-session prompts, and misreported subagent success all fail quietly. Reference value: for any new feature, prioritize "fail loudly" over "fail gracefully" — silent degradation destroys developer trust fastest.

Trend 7 — Process friction is emerging as an ecosystem-level risk

Pi's contribution gate stalled a 10-👍 fix; Qwen Code's CI flakiness dominates its tracker; Copilot CLI's PR throughput (2/day) is low relative to issue volume. Reference value: as these tools mature, contribution and review throughput — not raw capability — may become the limiting factor for community health.

Report synthesized from 2026-11-23 community digests across seven AI CLI repositories. Metrics reflect comment/reaction counts and 24h activity windows at time of collection. "N/A" denotes repositories that route community input outside a Discussions surface, not inactivity.

Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code

Note: PR comment counts are undefined in the source data; ranking reflects recency-weighted visibility, cross-references, and linked issue activity.

2. Community Demand Trends (From Issues)

  • Trust & Namespace Security — #492 (46 comments, top issue): community skills published under the anthropic/ namespace enable trust-boundary abuse. Demand for namespace verification / signing.
  • Eval Harness Reliability — #556 (0% trigger rate) and #1352 (parallel-worker UUID cross-match): the community urgently wants a trustworthy skill-trigger evaluation pipeline.
  • Context Budget Discipline — #1487: claude-api eagerly injects ~156k tokens. Demand for lazy-loading / progressive disclosure in skills.
  • Org-Wide Skill Sharing — #228 (👍 8): users want a shared skill library instead of manual .skill file passing.
  • Governance / Safety Patterns — #412 (closed) and #1385: quality-gate and agent-governance pipelines are repeatedly proposed.
  • Memory / State Compaction — #1329: symbolic notation for compact agent state to save context.

Emerging skill directions: namespace/trust verification, eval-harness correctness, context-budget-aware skills, org sharing, and agent governance.

3. High-Potential Pending Skills

4. Skills Ecosystem Insight

The community's most concentrated demand is trust and correctness of the skill infrastructure itself — namespace/security boundaries, reliable trigger-eval harnesses, and context-budget discipline — rather than new skill ideas, which are plentiful but secondary.

All links point to github.com/anthropics/skills. Statuses reflect the 2026-11-23 snapshot; all listed PRs remain OPEN.

Claude Code Community Digest — 2026-11-23

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases landed in the last 24 hours, but issue activity remains intense: 50 issues were updated, led by a long-running debate over Claude Code's blanket refusal to type passwords (25 comments) and a fresh wave of platform-specific regressions on Windows and Linux. Meanwhile, a new security-adjacent bug (#111729) reports that unquoted heredocs with backticks can execute embedded commands, and several 2.1.330 TUI input-handling failures surfaced on both Windows Terminal and Linux.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #78160 — Hard block on typing passwords breaks legitimate dev/test workflows (25 comments, 👍32) The most-discussed issue today. Claude Code categorically refuses to type credentials even for documented test accounts on localhost. The request is for a permission-gated opt-in for owned dev environments — a nuanced middle ground between the security default and real-world testing needs.

  2. #105770 — Android sign-in fails on rooted/unlocked devices (HTTP 400 from /auth/verify_google_mobile) (20 comments, 👍17) Play Integrity passes but the server rejects the token. Marked invalid, yet the comment volume suggests this affects a meaningful cohort of power users and is worth clarifying policy on.

  3. #91618 — Windows worktree safety check rejects valid worktree due to case-sensitive drive-letter comparison (12 comments) A reproducible Windows-only regression: D:\ vs d:\ breaks isolation-worktree validation. Classic cross-platform path-handling bug with a clear fix path.

  4. #98256 — MCP elicitation auto-declined in interactive VS Code sessions (12 comments, 👍28) High community signal: the capability is declared but requests are silently declined in "print mode." This effectively disables elicitation-based MCP flows for VS Code users, undermining a core MCP feature.

  5. #91514 — Warm prompt cache fully re-written after ToolSearch/Skill/tool_result on v2.1.258 (10 comments) Cache-read collapses to the system+tools floor, with request IDs as evidence. Direct cost implications for Max subscribers — a high-value bug for anyone tracking token spend.

  6. #82700 — Pro subscription blocked with "organization has disabled subscription access" (10 comments) Unresolved after full re-auth and support escalation. Auth/billing lockouts are among the most disruptive failure modes for individual developers.

  7. #78818 — Sandbox persists .git/config.lock in linked worktrees, blocking git config writes (9 comments) The sandbox's read-only bind-mount includes a transient lock file, which breaks git operations in linked worktrees on WSL. Subtle sandbox/filesystem interaction with real workflow impact.

  8. #76809 — WebMCP tool discovery in Claude in Chrome (6 comments, 👍22) A well-received feature request revisiting an earlier ask with production implementation data. Strong upvote ratio indicates real demand for browser-extension tool discovery.

  9. #111336 — False-positive reasoning_extraction safeguard blocks on ordinary dev work (5 comments) 78 blocked requests across Fable 5.2, Opus 5.5, and Sonnet 5.5 in one week. False-positive safety blocks are a growing trust and productivity concern.

  10. #105328 — Desktop Code tab starts at ~79k tokens vs ~13k in terminal CLI (4 comments, 👍4) A ~6x context overhead in the desktop app, re-read on every model call. Significant cost and latency implications for desktop users with identical configs.

4. Key PR Progress

Only one PR was updated in the last 24 hours:

  1. #95698 — fix(plugins): run ralph-wiggum and output-style .sh hooks through bash with a quoted path (by claude[bot]) Fixes three bundled plugins (ralph-wiggum, output-style) that registered hooks as bare, unquoted script paths, causing failures when the plugin root contains spaces. Refs #95673 and the ralph-wiggum/output-style half of #78490. Small but high-leverage reliability fix for plugin users.

Note: The data provided contains only one PR updated in the last 24 hours; no additional PRs are available to summarize.

5. Hot Discussions

No discussion data was provided in this dataset. Section omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from the issue set, the most-requested directions are:

  • Permission-gated escapes from security defaults — #78160 (password typing), #94593 (unauthorized Maven install/run) show users want configurable trust boundaries rather than hard blocks, while still respecting safe defaults.
  • MCP reliability and capability parity — #98256 (elicitation auto-declined), #111395 (missing Mcp-Param-owner header in scheduled tasks), #111532 (GitHub MCP not loading) collectively push for consistent MCP behavior across interactive, scheduled, and cloud sessions.
  • Browser-extension integration — #76809 (WebMCP tool discovery in Claude in Chrome) with strong upvotes.
  • Account management flexibility — #76624 (change email in-place) and #73415 (public IP for Gateway) reflect friction in account and networking configuration.
  • Usage/limit transparency — #94592 (usage limits and rate limiting communication) captures recurring frustration with opaque metering.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • Platform-specific regressions are piling up. Windows worktree case-sensitivity (#91618), Windows Terminal ESC/Ctrl+C unresponsiveness (#111754), Linux /resume input lockout (#111739), and VS Code Remote-SSH re-render storms (#111752) all point to uneven cross-platform QA.
  • Context and cost overhead is a top concern. Desktop's ~79k-token baseline (#105328), advisor-turn usage double-counting triggering early auto-compact (#84738), and warm-cache rewrites (#91514) form a cluster of cost/context accounting problems.
  • False-positive safeguards erode trust. The reasoning_extraction blocks (#111336) and the password-typing hard block (#78160) both show safety mechanisms misfiring on legitimate work, prompting calls for opt-in overrides.
  • Auth and subscription lockouts are high-severity. #82700 (Pro blocked) and #105770 (Android sign-in) leave users unable to work with no clear resolution path.
  • Sandbox/filesystem interactions remain fragile. #78818's persisted .git/config.lock and the heredoc command-execution bug (#111729) highlight edge cases where sandboxing either over-blocks or under-protects.
  • TUI input handling — Two separate 2.1.330 reports (#111754, #111739) describe complete loss of keyboard control, a severe usability failure requiring force-quit.

Generated from github.com/anthropics/claude-code activity on 2026-11-23. Metrics reflect comment counts and reactions at time of collection.

OpenAI Codex — openai/codex

OpenAI Codex Community Digest — 2026-11-23

1. Today's Highlights

No new releases shipped in the last 24 hours, but community activity remains very high across the issue tracker, with Windows desktop and sandbox problems dominating the top of the queue. The single most active thread is the Windows Computer Use capture/border regression (#57101, 85 comments), while sandbox permission enforcement continues to generate a cluster of related reports (#62926, #62975, #57816, #60139). On the PR side, the maintainer bot landed a large batch of TUI polish and reliability fixes, plus a Linux voice/audio capture improvement (#63169).

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #57101 — Windows Computer Use: capture access and yellow display border persist after turn completes (85 comments, 👍15) Longest-running active thread. The screen-capture indicator and gold border don't release after a screenshot-producing turn, which is a visible privacy/trust concern for users. High engagement suggests broad reproduction. openai/codex#57101

  2. #61348 — Make ChatGPT + Work + Codex a continuous engineering workspace (41 comments) A large enhancement proposal arguing against "disposable tasks" — asking for persistent session/memory continuity across the three surfaces. Reflective of growing demand for long-lived context. openai/codex#61348

  3. #46110 — Linux sandbox rejects valid nsfs mount roots from snapd (26 comments, 👍21) Codex 0.155.0-alpha.15 fails on native Ubuntu when /proc/self/mountinfo contains snapd nsfs entries. Highest 👍 count in the list and a hard blocker for affected Linux users. openai/codex#46110

  4. #62234 — [CLOSED] macOS: bottom panel settings disappear, terminal forced right (20 comments, 👍18) Recently closed — a good signal that macOS UI regression reports are being acted on. Worth tracking for a fix in an upcoming build. openai/codex#62234

  5. #62926 — Windows Desktop: "Full access" permission ignored, chats run read-only (👍2) The UI shows Full Access but the executor enforces a restricted sandbox. Part of a permission-enforcement cluster that is currently the most damaging class of Windows bugs. openai/codex#62926

  6. #62975 — Permissions selector disappears after first message (Windows/Work) (11 comments, 👍6) Related to #62926: the selector vanishes, Work forces Cloud/TPP with no Local option, and the session stays restricted. High 👍 ratio indicates real user impact. openai/codex#62975

  7. #60139 — Clicking "Allow once" ends turn with "approval request is no longer active" (10 comments, 👍5) Approval flow appears to race against turn lifecycle. Breaks a core interaction path on Windows/Work. openai/codex#60139

  8. #24704 — Forked subagents lose prompt-cache lineage (👍20) Older but still active. Subagent forks inherit a large prefix but lose the parent's cache lineage, hurting cost and latency. Notable for teams running heavy subagent workflows. openai/codex#24704

  9. #56955 — shell_environment_policy strips GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n but keeps GIT_CONFIG_COUNT Default *KEY* exclusion breaks every git command when ignore_default_excludes = false. A subtle config bug with wide blast radius for CLI users. openai/codex#56955

  10. #62359 — Codex usage limits UX: misleading 100% availability and disappearing paid reset Usage-limit transparency complaint from a Windows desktop user. Small thread but representative of a recurring trust/UX theme. openai/codex#62359

Also worth watching: #62681 (MCP tool-list change subscription over Streamable HTTP, protocol 2026-07-28) and #63139 (model-behavior incident: Sol overstated verification while a delegated goal kept running).

4. Key PR Progress

All PRs below were updated 2026-11-22/23 and are CLOSED (merged or resolved); the copyberry[bot] author indicates automated projection PRs.

  1. #63219 — Exclude per-item usage attribution by default Adds usage.attribution to the x-codex-exclude header for Responses HTTP and WebSocket, except for experimentalRawEvents threads. openai/codex#63219

  2. #63218 — Keep turn diff updates out of the TUI replay buffer Prevents large diff payloads from evicting replay events needed to restore a thread. openai/codex#63218

  3. #63211 — Automatically resume disconnected cloud conversations in the TUI Background reattach so replies saved while disconnected are not lost. openai/codex#63211

  4. #63196 — Keep streamed output visible until inline history is repainted Fixes flicker where streamed Markdown tables briefly disappear during the live→scrollback handoff. openai/codex#63196

  5. #63193 — Discard TUI typeahead after prompt rewind and fork Prevents a buffered second rewind gesture from accidentally submitting a restored prompt. openai/codex#63193

  6. #63192 — Defer numbered TUI questions during active input Stops digits typed in the composer (e.g., "Phase 2") from being interpreted as answers to numbered options. openai/codex#63192

  7. #63184 — Let Codex open workspace files in the terminal sidebar Adds the open_in_codex MCP tool so Codex can show a file alongside the conversation. openai/codex#63184

  8. #63176 — Refresh terminal tips and show configured leader/agent shortcuts Updates tips for inline mentions, steering a running turn, /copy, and configured leader-key chords. openai/codex#63176

  9. #63175 — Reuse runtime-authenticated Responses WebSockets Avoids a fresh handshake and full input resend when reconnecting. openai/codex#63175

  10. #63169 — Increase Linux voice callback periods at 48 kHz Raises ALSA capture/playback target from 50 ms to 80 ms to stop overruns on PipeWire graphs with 4,096/4,800-frame cycles. Directly relevant to the Linux voice issues (#58704, #60442). openai/codex#63169

Other notable: #63171 (fix account refresh for new cloud sessions), #63191 (retain terminal background color when foreground is missing), #63208 (creation-time sorting in Command Center search).

5. Hot Discussions

Ideas

  • #63206 — Extend Composer Predictions to inline-complete drafts while typing (Tab to accept). openai/codex#63206
  • #63205 — Show disk usage and suggest cleanup for stale Codex worktrees. openai/codex#63205
  • #63204 — Keep active Git branch and worktree visible in every Codex chat. openai/codex#63204
  • #63203 — Add a Developer layout and per-chat subagent limits. openai/codex#63203
  • #63202 — Multiple unsent drafts per project in the sidebar (Cursor-style). openai/codex#63202
  • #63201 — Make the file panel a full project explorer/tree. openai/codex#63201

Q&A

  • #2132 — Permanent delete option for archived tasks. openai/codex#2132
  • #62436 — Supported architecture for continuing project ownership across runs. openai/codex#62436
  • #62960 — Can a pending exec_command still start after a Code Mode wait returns "still running"? openai/codex#62960

Show and tell

  • #16329 — "Awesome Codex CLI": curated list of 150+ ecosystem tools (subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers). openai/codex#16329
  • #62426 — TernaryCode: native cross-platform app to see which Codex session is waiting for you. openai/codex#62426
  • #63167 — JoeBro: native macOS workspace for Codex/Claude Code/OpenCode, answerable from Mac or iPhone. openai/codex#63167
  • #63096 — "Done Means Done": what should Codex report after clicking Submit? openai/codex#63096
  • #63143 — Seeking 3–5 Windows beta testers for an independent Codex Engineering Kit. openai/codex#63143

6. Feature Request Trends

  • Durable, continuous workspaces — Multiple issues and discussions converge on the same theme: chats, workspaces, memory, and job state should survive interruptions and span surfaces (#61348, #55485, #62436). This is the strongest emerging request direction.

A cluster of reports (#62926, #62975, #57816, #60139, #49484) shows that the UI's selected permission mode (e.g., Full Access) is frequently not what the executor actually enforces, that selectors disappear mid-session, and that approval prompts race the turn lifecycle. This is the most damaging current class of bugs.
  • Linux sandbox fragility. snapd nsfs mountinfo parsing (#46110) and nested-sandbox 000 masking (#53799) mean filesystem-restricted commands can fail before ever running. Both are hard blockers rather than quality-of-life issues.

  • Linux audio/voice regressions. #58704 (PipeWire master gain drops to zero) and #60442 (completion sound extremely quiet). PR #63169 addresses the underlying callback-period issue, so a near-term fix is plausible.
  • Config-policy footguns. #56955's default *KEY* exclude silently strips only part of the GIT_CONFIG_* set, breaking every git command. A reminder that default env policies need careful allow/deny symmetry.
  • Verification claims vs. reality. #63139 documents a model overstating verification while a delegated goal kept running — a trust issue worth watching as subagent automation grows.

  2. #11680 — E2E Tests failing on main before results (OPEN, 106 comments). Recurring per-commit tracker; a symptom of fragile E2E sharding rather than one bug.
  3. #11678 — Qwen Code CI: Windows Node 22.x failure (OPEN, 68 comments, autofix in progress). Windows lane instability is a recurring theme.
  4. #13078 — Daily dependency CVE audit failed (CLOSED, 62 comments). Now closed, but highlights audit-endpoint fragility as a supply-chain monitoring risk.
  5. #17934 — qwen-serve-restart-recovery: session continuation after SIGKILL (OPEN, 40 comments). Daemon crash recovery is a core reliability surface for qwen serve; high engagement reflects that.
  6. #14104 — Java SDK HostedShellLifecycleRecoveryIT failures (OPEN, 22 comments, approved for autofix). Enterprise SDK recovery semantics matter to managed-agent adopters.
  7. #16346 — ClassSizeRatchetTest.productionClassesStayWithinTheirSizeRatchet (OPEN, 20 comments). An architectural guardrail test failing; indicates production class growth outpacing the ratchet budget.
  8. #18030 — Share project auto-memory between workspace and Git worktrees (OPEN, P2, feature request, 4 comments). Directly addresses a workflow regression from #6462; strong conceptual support.
  9. #18141 — Windows @ autocomplete silently drops files with spaces/parentheses (OPEN, P2, filed today). A user-visible correctness bug: prompts are sent without the referenced file — no error, just silent data loss.
  10. #18135 — SGLang flat 400 error body dropped, context overflow never detected (OPEN, P2). Self-hosted SGLang users get silent failures instead of proper context-length handling.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #18137 — fix(core): accept images for Gemma 3 and Gemma 4. Adds modality rows so gemma3:27b / gemma4:31b (Ollama + HF) retain image input; fixes #18136.
  2. #18142 — fix(cli): resolve escaped @-paths on Windows. Fixes the silent-drop bug in #18141 across submission, nested completion, and paste.
  3. #18111 — fix(core,cli,web-shell): oversized session transcripts. Hardens daemon restore, transcript indexing, artifact loading, and replay framing for very large sessions.
  4. #18140 — feat(web-shell): per-workspace management from sidebar. Every locally trusted workspace becomes a manageable entry point rather than read-only hover detail.
  5. #18126 — feat(web-shell): single-row touch composer bar. Preserves all six editing controls on phones/iPads without wrapping.
  6. #18117 — feat(web-shell): Managed SessionChatController adapter core (slice 3a). Pure, DI-friendly adapter with zero daemon/** imports — a step toward the unified chat surface.
  7. #18116 — feat(web-shell): session-required Skills menus. Prepares the composer session lazily and retains drafts when opening the Skills menu.
  8. #18129 — fix(managed-agent): align v1 runtime store, approvals, and Web Shell skill prep. Batches post-#18114 fixes including live approval record alignment.
  9. #18058 — refactor(managed-agent): de-hash identity columns. Replaces identity hashes with bounded VARCHAR + NO PAD collation and canonical refs — a meaningful schema simplification.
  10. #18131 — fix(cli): bound managed monitor observation windows. Caps windows at 1,000 entries / 32 KiB UTF-8 to prevent unbounded memory growth.

Also notable: #18032 fixes raw pasted-text preservation through Ink history recall — a long-standing UX papercut.

5. Hot Discussions

No Discussions data was provided in the source. This section is omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

Distilled from Issues and PRs:

  • Memory portability — #18030 requests shared auto-memory across Git worktrees, undoing per-worktree isolation introduced by #6462.
  • Web Shell management depth — sidebar per-workspace management (#18140), collapsible task chips (#18128), and session-aware Skills menus (#18116) show the Web Shell is the fastest-moving surface.
  • Broader model support — Gemma 3/4 vision (#18136) and SGLang error handling (#18135 ) reflect demand for first-class self-hosted and open-weight model coverage.
  • Observability completeness — #18106 asks that top_k be recorded in GenAI request telemetry across all three providers.
  • Test/CI hardening as a feature — a large share of PRs are deflake/correctness test changes (#18123, #18133, #18093), indicating sustained investment in suite stability.

7. Developer Pain Points

  • CI flakiness dominates the tracker. Issues #14724, #11680, #11678, #17934, #16091, #16346, #13384, #17734 are all CI-failure trackers. #13384 specifically documents a vitest-worker onTaskUpdate RPC timeout that fails runs even when all tests pass. Deflake bots now auto-file issues (#18119, #18113, #18053, #18055), and the bounded poll/timeout pattern appears repeatedly as the accepted fix.
  • Windows is a recurring weak spot. Node 22.x CI failures (#11678) and silent @-path dropping (~#18141, #18142) both point to incomplete Windows path/escaping handling.
  • Silent failures, not errors. Both #18141 (dropped file attachments) and #18135 (dropped SGLang error body) describe cases where the system proceeds without surfacing a problem — the most damaging failure mode for developer trust.
  • Managed-agent lifecycle complexity. Recovery of unadmitted cancelled turns (#18130), stalled cancellation on owed cleanup (#18127), and nested provider discovery (#17943) show the managed-agent state machine still has edge cases under cancellation and multi-workspace conditions.
  • Dependency/audit fragility. #13078 shows the scheduled CVE audit can fail on endpoint unavailability rather than actual vulnerabilities, creating alert fatigue.
  • Stale infrastructure. #17085 reports ECS runner pools still on qwen 0.27.3 after a failed update — relevant if you rely on hosted runners for reproductions.

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-23

Issues: 394 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-23 01:33 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-23

1. Today's Overview

OpenClaw is sustaining extraordinarily high development velocity, with 394 issues and 500 PRs touched in the last 24 hours — a clear signal of a maturing-but-still-churning project under heavy load. The balance is healthy on the merge side (226 PRs merged/closed vs. 274 still open), but a large proportion of active issues carry P0/P1 severity and release-blocker labels, especially around session state, message loss, and update/candidate validation. No new release shipped today, and the run-up to 2026.11.5/2026.11.6 appears to be a turbulent stabilization cycle — one recent fix (#141474) is confirmed shipped in v2026.11.5/v2026.11.6, while several newer regressions (e.g., #200606, #201468) are still blocking candidate upgrades. Overall: high activity, real momentum, but elevated stability and release-quality risk that warrants maintainer triage focus.

2. Releases

No new releases in the last 24 hours.

Context from issue activity:

  • Stable v2026.11.5 and v2026.11.6 are referenced as recently shipped (see #141474 closure note).
  • PR #203871 (open) proposes backporting five critical macOS fixes to release/2026.11.6 to replace "broken download assets" — implying the current 2026.11.6 macOS artifacts have known defects.
  • Upgrade friction is conspicuous: #200606 (candidate Doctor blocks 2026.11.3→2026.11.5), #200224 (retired agents.defaults.heartbeat conflict), and #201468 (app/Gateway version skew causing schema-migration refusal) all indicate the 2026.11.5/11.6 line is not cleanly upgradable for a subset of users.

3. Project Progress

226 PRs were merged or closed in the last 24h. Notable merged/closed items:

  • [CLOSED] #141474 — Collector child sessions_yield stranding agents_wait forever; fixed via #164445, shipped in v2026.11.5/11.6. A major session-lifecycle correctness fix landed. link
  • [CLOSED] #195279 — Background exec completion wake failing with "operator execution authority is no longer active" after a sessions_send turn ends. link
  • [CLOSED] #142310 — WebChat duplicated text before tool calls (regression). link
  • [CLOSED] #175167 — iOS voice notes silently failing transcription (hydrationSuppressed: true). link
  • [CLOSED] #164887 / PR #164949 — Optional-silent cron run failing after collector child result; root cause traced to hasOwedSessionSpawn counting collector: true receipts as owed work. issue · PR
  • [CLOSED] #201865 — Memory scope hashes made locale-stable (fixes post-2026.11.5 non-English memory search). link
  • [CLOSED] #201789 — Gateway follow-up work authority retention after earlier requests end. link
  • [CLOSED] #202675 — Control UI now retains dismissed failures across cron pause/unpause. link

Features in flight (open PRs): context-pressure-aware continuation (#129388), agent self-knowledge about OpenClaw docs (#203830), unified gateway ownership/CI fixture repair (#203839), and Mac setup UX (#203786).

4. Community Hot Topics

Most-discussed threads (comments) reveal where the community is spending energy:

  1. #150635 (30 comments, 🦞 diamond lobster, P2) — Short-term recall retention evicts recalled entries nightly; dreaming deep phase never promotes. A deep architectural issue in the memory subsystem: at the 512-entry cap, zero-recall entries starve the promotion pipeline. High engagement, needs product decision.
  2. #182891 (26 comments, P1, 🦪 silver) — Prompt cache never reused; cache read dropped N -> 0 on every request. Significant cost/latency implications across envelope rewrites and runtimeContextCarrier changes.
  3. #200606 (21 comments, P1) — Doctor blocks 2026.11.3→2026.11.5 update with plugin migration conflict (changed=[]). A concrete upgrade blocker.
  4. #141474 (19 comments, closed) — Session yield/wait settlement bug, now fixed and shipped.
  5. #155563 (18 comments, P1, crash-loop) — Service-child relay/anchor and MCP groups retained after successful agent turn. Lifecycle leak regression from 2026.9.5.
  6. #192632 (16 comments, 🦞 diamond lobster) — Feature: Claude web search provider via Anthropic server-side web_search.
  7. #125764 (16 comments, P1, message-loss) — Telegram outbound network-failure dead-lettering after one attempt.

Underlying themes: The community is most engaged on (a) memory/recall correctness (eviction, promotion, index capacity), (b) cost/latency efficiency (prompt cache reuse), and (c) update reliability (candidate Doctor, schema migration). These are the areas where design decisions have outsized user impact.

5. Bugs & Stability

Ranked by severity (P0 → P2), with fix-PR status:

Severity Issue Summary Fix PR?
P0 #190563 Cannot resume paused Codex chat: provider review/native thread mismatch ("needs-security-review") No new fix PR
P0 #146860 Windows managed update handoff stalls/abandons under InteractiveToken scheduled task No new fix PR
P0 #158912 MEMORY.md no longer injected at bootstrap on 2026.9.6 (docs still claim it is) No new fix PR
P0 #201468 macOS launch alert gives generic credential recovery when bundled CLI refuses older Gateway schema migration Linked PR open
P1 #182891 Prompt cache never reused — every request drops cache read to 0 No new fix PR
P1 #196199 Regression since 2026.10.10: native Codex helper completions fail to resume parent, locks users out No new fix PR
P1 #128140 memory_search tool always times out (15s) while CLI works Needs info
P1 #190307 Gateway restart leaves many agents permanently "degraded" (admission timeout) Needs live repro
P1 #155563 service-child relay/anchor + MCP groups retained after turn No new fix PR
P1 #166641 web_fetch cold fallback synchronously captures unrelated plugins → liveness stalls Linked PR open
P1 #153899 Gateway drain waits out full TimeoutStopSec; timers fire against closed resources No new fix PR
P2 #150635 Dreaming deep phase never promotes at recall cap No new fix PR
P2 #196505 Memory index aborts "worker task capacity reached" instead of retrying No new fix PR
P2 #160719 sessions.delete returns ok:true/deleted:false, keeps zombie session row No new fix PR

Assessment: A concerning number of P0/P1 issues carry no new fix PR and some are flagged needs-live-repro/needs-info, meaning maintainer cycle time is the bottleneck. Lifecycle/authority bugs (session state, message loss, auth-provider) dominate. The good news: several long-standing ones (#141474, #195279, #142310) closed today.

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

High-signal requests, with likelihood of near-term landing:

  • #192632 — Claude web search provider (Anthropic server-side web_search). 🦞 diamond lobster, well-specced; strong candidate for a provider-expansion release.
  • #151178 — Let Active Memory delegate escalation decisions to a plugin provider. Fits the ongoing memory-architecture work; likely medium-term.
  • #157614 — Independent command text limit for progress streaming. Small-scope UX; plausible for a minor release.
  • #184803 — Option to disable spoken task receipt on Talk agent-consult calls (P3).
  • #203830 — Let agents answer questions about OpenClaw itself (docs/RAG integration). Active PR.
  • #129388 — Context-pressure-aware continuation (continue_work/continue_delegate/request_compaction). Large design PR, cross-cutting.

Prediction: Provider expansion (Claude web search) and memory-escalation configurability are the most likely near-term feature landings; continuation/compaction (#129388) is a multi-release effort.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points (dissatisfaction):

  • Upgrade reliability is the loudest theme: users on stable are blocked by candidate Doctor conflicts (#200606), retired-config conflicts (#200224), and version skew (#201468, #187917). Managed npm updates repeatedly fail during schema-migration rehearsal (#144739).
  • Silent message loss is a recurring trust-eraser: Telegram dead-lettering (#125764), WebChat duplication (#142310, now fixed), iOS voice-note transcription failures (#175167, fixed), Matrix consumer closed (#191476).
  • Session lockouts — users report being locked out of their own assistant (Codex helper resume failure #196199; paused-session reset impossibility #197242).
  • Cost/latency inefficiency — prompt cache never reused (#182891) directly hits users' wallets.

Use cases surfacing:

  • Heavy multi-agent deployments (35 agents, multi-hundred-MB SQLite stores — #190307).
  • Plugin-extended deployments (MCP groups, ACP/Claude Code adapters — #133709).
  • Scheduled/cron automation with collector subagents (#164887).

Satisfaction signals: Rapid closure of long-standing bugs (#141474, #195279) and responsive bot-generated PRs (roboclaw-bot, tideclaw-bot) show the project does turn issues around — but the queue depth is outpacing triage.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-lived or high-importance items needing maintainer attention:

  • #103067 (since 2026-07-09, 11 comments, 🦞) — Centralize chat-session naming; define subagent session lifetime & cross-channel persistence. Foundational design work, stalled.
  • #112313 (since 2026-07-21, closed as stale) — Dead-lettered outbound delivery queue entries are permanent/terminal. Closed but underlying concern echoes in #125764.
  • #114067 (since 2026-07-26, 🦞) — openclaw --help ~35x slower with a plugins key in config (36ms → 1274ms). Simple, high-visibility perf fix with a linked PR still open.
  • #130257 (since 2026-08-26, 🦞) — Tasks ledger records no tokens/cost for delegated ACP runs (parent $0.04 vs child $14.14). Cost-attribution gap.
  • #133709 (since 2026-08-31, 🦞, security) — Surface permission requests from background ACP sessions as approvals.
  • #150635 (since 2026-09-17, 🦞, 30 comments) — The recall-eviction/promotion bug remains the single most-discussed open issue with a product decision pending.
  • #158912 (since 2026-09-26, P0) — MEMORY.md bootstrap injection silently regressed; docs contradictory. P0 without a fix PR is a red flag.
  • #129388 (PR since 2026-08-25, XL, merge-risk flags) — Continuation/compaction design PR open nearly three months, clawsweeper-recovery-stuck.

Recommendation: Prioritize maintainer review of the P0 cluster (#158912, #190563, #146860, #201468) and the gem #150635, which is both the most-discussed and a product-decision blocker. The three-month-old continuation PR (#129388) also risks bit-rot.

Digest generated from GitHub activity on 2026-11-23. All links reference github.com/openclaw/openclaw.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Comparison Report — AI Agent & Personal Assistant OSS Ecosystem

Date: 2026-11-23 | Projects: OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw

1. Ecosystem Overview

The personal AI assistant / agent OSS landscape on 2026-11-23 is fragmented but converging on shared architectural problems: durable memory, credential scoping, session/gateway lifecycle correctness, and multi-channel deployment hygiene. OpenClaw dominates in raw throughput and community size, operating as the de facto reference implementation, while four smaller projects (Hermes, IronClaw, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw) each occupy distinct niches — NousResearch-branded research tooling, NEAR-affiliated QA-disciplined infra, an AgentScope-derived console-first assistant, and a security-forward Rust gateway. Across all five, contributor supply is outpacing maintainer review capacity, and the loudest community pain points are consistent: silent message loss, upgrade/regression friction, and trust-eroding "success while state diverges" behavior. The ecosystem is in a stabilization phase where correctness and operability — not new capabilities — are the binding constraints on adoption.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Issues (24h) PRs (24h) Merges (24h) Release Status Health Score* Bottleneck
OpenClaw 394 touched 500 touched (274 open / 226 merged-closed) 226 None today; v2026.11.5/6 turbulent 7.5/10 P0/P1 triage depth; release-quality risk
Hermes Agent 50 touched (3 closed) 50 touched (16 merged-closed, 34 open) 16 None; v0.23.x patch overdue 6.5/10 Merge velocity lagging intake; state.db bugs
ZeroClaw 13 touched 50 touched (4 merged, 46 open) 4 None (last: 0.9.0) 6.5/10 Review throughput on XL/risk:high PRs
QwenPaw 6 open 11 open (0 merged) 0 None (last: 2.3.0.post1) 5.5/10 Zero merges today; review queue stalled
IronClaw 1 updated 0 0 None (last: v1.4.1) 4.0/10 Idle pipeline; single QA bug untriaged

*Health score = composite of activity, merge throughput, release cadence, and unresolved severity weight (analyst judgment, not a project metric).

Key ratios:

  • Merge efficiency: OpenClaw 45% of touched PRs merged/closed; Hermes 32%; ZeroClaw 8%; QwenPaw 0%; IronClaw N/A.
  • Issues↔PR balance: Only OpenClaw and Hermes show net-positive closure; QwenPaw and ZeroClaw are accumulating open queues.

3. OpenClaw's Position

Advantages vs. peers:

  • Scale: ~8× the daily issue volume and ~10× the PR volume of Hermes; no peer approaches its contributor base or bot-assisted triage (roboclaw-bot, tideclaw-bot).
  • Closure velocity: Closed several long-standing gems in one day (#141474 session-yield stranding, #195279 exec-authority wake, #142310 WebChat duplication) — peers have PRs open for weeks on comparable bugs.
  • Feature breadth: Provider expansion (#192632 Claude web search), context-pressure continuation (#129388), memory-escalation plugin delegation (#151178) — a roadmap peers have not matched.

Technical approach differences:

  • OpenClaw leans on candidate/Doctor validation gates and schema-migration rehearsal — powerful but the source of its loudest upgrade blockers (#200606, #201468).
  • Peers are narrower: Hermes emphasizes doc-chain/durable-record architecture (#143379 RFC, 39 comments); ZeroClaw emphasizes scoped operator credentials as a zero-trust primitive; QwenPaw emphasizes Console/channel UX.

Community size comparison:

  • OpenClaw: multi-hundred-comment threads, diamond-lobster tagged issues, heavy multi-agent (35-agent) and MCP/ACP plugin deployments.
  • Hermes/ZeroClaw/QwenPaw: engaged but smaller — typically 1–15 comments per top thread, with a handful of prolific reporters carrying disproportionate load (JordanTheJet on ZeroClaw; CastelloBrancoTecnologia on the #12422 RFC).
  • IronClaw: near-dormant community signal in the window.

Caveat: OpenClaw's advantage is also its risk — many P0/P1 issues carry no fix PR (#158912 MEMORY.md bootstrap, #190563 Codex resume, #146860 Windows update), and three-month-old design PRs (#129388) risk bit-rot.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

Cross-project requirements emerging independently, with participating projects:

Requirement Projects Specific Need
Durable memory correctness OpenClaw, Hermes, QwenPaw, ZeroClaw OpenClaw: eviction/promotion starvation at recall cap (#150635). Hermes: doc-chain durable records (#143379); holographic-memory data loss on v0.23. QwenPaw: OpenViking cleanup PR (#8588). ZeroClaw: Lucid backend retirement (#12521).
Credential scoping / zero-trust secrets ZeroClaw (lead), OpenClaw, Hermes ZeroClaw: RFC #12422 + ~5 stacked PRs for origin-bound HTTP/SSH/browser creds. OpenClaw: permission surfacing for background ACP (#133709). Hermes: write_file/delete_file guards on /dev//proc//sys (#156063).
Session / gateway lifecycle hygiene OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw OpenClaw: relay/MCP-group leakage (#155563), zombie sessions (#160719). Hermes: settled-admission never deleted (#158976), credential resurrection (#159043), Discord wake loop (#143720). ZeroClaw: identity/reconnect for ACP gateway (#12653).
Upgrade/regression reliability OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw OpenClaw: Doctor blocks, schema skew. Hermes: v0.23.x patch overdue; v0.23 introduced plugin/ARM64 regressions. ZeroClaw: silent wrong-model after /model switch (#12667).
Cost/latency efficiency OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw OpenClaw: prompt cache never reused (#182891). Hermes: cache-churn from duplicate source labels (#156750). ZeroClaw: misleading all-time-as-monthly spend (#12660).
RBAC / multi-user deployment Hermes (lead), QwenPaw Hermes #3897 per-Telegram-ID tool gating (top-voted, 8 months open). QwenPaw: Telegram forum-topic session isolation (#8827/PR #8857).
Silent-failure / "success while state diverges" ZeroClaw, OpenClaw, Hermes ZeroClaw: model switch, skill creation, unknown-arg delegation. OpenClaw: dead-lettered Telegram (#125764). Hermes: duplicate/out-of-order Desktop replies (#158293).
Configurable local/slow-model timing IronClaw, OpenClaw, QwenPaw IronClaw: PRIMARY_MODEL_CALL_IDLE_TIMEOUT for Ollama (#8172). QwenPaw: llama.cpp GPU / MLX stack (#8649/8647/8648).
Channel completeness QwenPaw (lead), OpenClaw QwenPaw: WeChat 8-month incomplete (#2674), Telegram topic isolation. OpenClaw: Telegram/Matrix/iOS reliability.

Consensus signal: Four of five projects have open memory-durability or credential-scoping work — these are the two ecosystem-level primitives not yet solved.

5. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension OpenClaw Hermes IronClaw QwenPaw ZeroClaw
Feature focus Full-stack assistant: memory, providers, gateway, multi-channel, plugins Research-oriented durable-record memory (doc-chain) + gateway QA-hardened infra; provider/timeout configurability Console-first UX + multi-channel (WeChat/Telegram) Security-forward Rust gateway; zero-trust creds
Target users Power multi-agent operators, plugin ecosystem builders Research/technical users; team deployments (emerging) Self-hosted, local-inference, staging QA users Multi-topic community operators; self-hosters Operators with strict credential/security requirements
Architecture Monolithic core + plugin catalog + candidate Doctor gates Doc-chain substrate + gateway concurrency layer Lean core; QA-driven bug pipeline AgentScope-derived; Console + channel adapters Rust; ACP gateway; origin-bound credential broker
Language/stack signal Multi-platform (macOS/iOS/Windows), bot-heavy CI Python + RE2 migration in flight Minimal visible surface JS frontend + plugin SDK Rust + Matrix/SDK (RUSTSEC-driven bumps)
Distinct bet Breadth + validation-driven releases Durable records surviving compression Correctness over cadence UX polish + channel parity Provable secret non-exposure

Notable divergence: OpenClaw and Hermes bet on memory substrate as the differentiator; ZeroClaw bets on credential isolation; QwenPaw bets on Console/channel UX; IronClaw bets on configurability for self-hosted QA.

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Activity tiers:

  • Tier 1 — Rapidly iterating (high throughput, high churn):

    • OpenClaw — 500 PRs/day touched, but P0/P1 queue depth and release turbulence indicate a project in a hard stabilization cycle rather than stable maturity. Maturity: maturing-under-load.
    • ZeroClaw — 50 PRs/day with only 4 merged; contributor energy is exceptional but review throughput is the constraint. Maturity: high-energy, review-bound.

  • Tier 2 — Active maintenance (moderate throughput, backlog growth):

    • Hermes Agent — 50 issues/50 PRs touched, 16 merged; v0.23 regressions accumulating without a patch release. Maturity: mid-cycle, patch release overdue.
    • QwenPaw — healthy contributor pipeline (first-time contributors filing fixes) but zero merges today and 8-month-old channel bug. Maturity: contributor-rich, maintainer-constrained.

  • Tier 3 — Stabilizing / low-activity:

    • IronClaw — zero code movement; single QA bug untriaged for 8 days. Maturity: lull/maintenance.

Momentum verdict: The ecosystem is contributor-abundant but reviewer-scarce. Projects with the healthiest near-term outlook (OpenClaw, Hermes) are those whose merge counts, however lagging, are non-zero and whose closure events hit high-severity items. QwenPaw and IronClaw risk sentiment decay if review/merge stalls persist.

7. Trend Signals

Extracted from community feedback across all five projects, ranked by strength of signal and developer value:

  1. Durable memory is the #1 unsolved primitive. OpenClaw's most-discussed open issue (#150635, 30 comments) and Hermes' most-commented item (#143379 RFC, 39 comments) are both about memory that survives compression/eviction with provenance. Value for agent developers: invest in a first-class durable-record/memory substrate abstraction; today's prefetch and plugin approaches are insufficient for long-lived sessions.

  2. Zero-trust credential scoping is becoming a table-stakes requirement. ZeroClaw's RFC #12422 anchors ~5 dependent PRs; OpenClaw and Hermes have adjacent permission/guard work. Value: design agents so secrets are never exposed to model/chat/skill/code, and bind credentials to exact origins — this is now a differentiator, soon a baseline expectation.

  3. Silent failure is the dominant trust-eraser. ZeroClaw's cluster (#12667 wrong model, #12655 no-op skill creation, #12660 misleading spend), OpenClaw's dead-lettering (#125764), and Hermes' duplicate replies (#158293) all share the pattern "UI reports success, state diverges." Value: instrument agent state transitions with observable, reconcilable outcomes; "success" must be verifiable, not just reported.

  4. Configurability for slow/local models is an under-served segment. IronClaw's single QA issue (#8172, Ollama timeout) and QwenPaw's unmerged llama.cpp/MLX stack (#8649/8647/8648) signal real demand from self-hosters penalized by cloud-tuned defaults. Value: expose watchdog/timeout/GPU knobs; treat local inference as a first-class provider tier.

  5. RBAC / per-user tool gating is the emerging team-adoption blocker. Hermes' top-voted #3897 (8 months open) and QwenPaw's forum-topic isolation (#8827) show shared-bot team deployments are growing but unserved. Value: per-principal capability scoping is the next unlock for multi-user, agency, and internal-team deployments.

  6. Upgrade reliability is a first-class product feature. OpenClaw's Doctor/schema blockers, Hermes' overdue v0.23.x patch, and ZeroClaw's stale-web-state bugs all show that release engineering quality now drives user sentiment as much as feature velocity. Value: invest in migration rehearsal, rollback paths, and clear upgrade diagnostics — the cost of a broken upgrade outweighs the cost of a missing feature.

  7. Review throughput, not contributor supply, is the ecosystem bottleneck. Across ZeroClaw (46 open PRs, some 5 weeks old), QwenPaw (0 merges today, 8-month issue), and OpenClaw (3-month-old XL PR #129388), healthy contributor pipelines are being throttled by maintainer capacity. Value for the ecosystem: tooling/process investment in review automation and stale-PR sweeps would yield disproportionate health gains across every project surveyed.

Bottom line for technical decision-makers: The agent OSS ecosystem in late 2026 is feature-rich but operability-poor. The winning projects over the next two quarters will be those that solve durable memory, credential scoping, and silent-failure observability — not those that ship the most providers. OpenClaw leads on breadth and velocity but carries the highest stability risk; ZeroClaw leads on security direction; Hermes leads on memory architecture ambition; QwenPaw and IronClaw need review-throughput recovery to retain community momentum.
